rationale: Evidence from the development race (entityR2A, 60 trials, 0 finishes): every trial ended off_track on all three tracks. Progress was only 0.075 to 0.16, so the robot left the line early in each course. rms_error was small (about 0.026 m), but max_error reached about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m). The failures are therefore brief excursions at the bends, not drift. Line_loss_events of 1 to 2 per run and steering_oscillation of about 0.14 both point to an aggressive loop: base_speed 1.6 is too fast for the bends, and kd 0.3 is too weak to damp the overshoot. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.25 so the robot can corner inside the off-track limit. Speed is the main risk, and a finish needs only about 1.5 m/s average, so I accept a slower run for now. (2) kd 0.3 to 0.8 to damp the oscillation seen in steering_oscillation. (3) kp 5.0 to 6.0 to keep the robot tight on the line through the bends. The extra kp is partly offset by the lower speed, which reduces the lateral reaction needed. (4) ki 0.05 to 0.02 to reduce integral windup on the long bends. (5) Mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia, so the robot turns more quickly to correct errors. (6) Sensors moved from y=0.04 to y=0.05 to give slightly more lead before each bend. Expected result: no off-track events on the oval or s-bend, possibly completion on the oval; progress should rise well above 0.16. Hypotheses: (a) the off-track events are caused by speed at bends, so lower speed plus higher kd should cut max_error below 0.06; (b) if line_loss_events stay at 1 or more, the sensors are losing the tape at sharp bends and a wider sensor footprint or more forward sensors would help; (c) if steering_oscillation is still high, kd is still too low or kp too high. Measurements wanted next: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error and line_loss_events on each track, plus steering_oscillation to test whether the kd change damps the jitter.
